ccw-cube.text: Replace the cube's 36 vertices with a cube whose every triangle is counter-clockwise when you look at its face from outside; keep each vertex's texture coordinates.
ccw-cube.hint: In learnopengl's cube the back, right and top faces are clockwise from outside: swap the 2nd and 3rd corner of each of their triangles. Check: (b − a) × (c − a) points out of the cube. Nothing visible changes yet.

text.opengl: Enable face culling: `glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE)`, cull the back faces (`glCullFace(GL_BACK)`) with counter-clockwise front faces (`glFrontFace(GL_CCW)`), and make the floor's triangles counter-clockwise seen from above.
text.vulkan: Cull the back faces: `rasterizer.cullMode = VK_CULL_MODE_BACK_BIT` with `rasterizer.frontFace = VK_FRONT_FACE_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE`, and make the floor's triangles counter-clockwise seen from above.
text.d3d12: Cull the back faces: `CullMode = D3D12_CULL_MODE_BACK` with `FrontCounterClockwise = TRUE` in `psoDesc.RasterizerState`, and make the floor's triangles counter-clockwise seen from above.

hint.opengl: The three calls go after `glDepthFunc` (the last two are the defaults). learnopengl's `planeVertices` are clockwise from above: swap the 2nd and 3rd vertex of both triangles, or the floor vanishes.
hint.vulkan: The y flip in the projection (`proj[1][1] *= -1`) shows the scene upright, so counter-clockwise from outside is counter-clockwise on screen, as in OpenGL. Floor: swap the 2nd and 3rd vertex of both triangles.
hint.d3d12: Replace the `D3D12_CULL_MODE_NONE` line. With the right-handed matrices the screen looks like OpenGL's, so counter-clockwise is the front. Floor: swap the 2nd and 3rd vertex of both triangles.

text.vulkan: Cull the front faces instead: `rasterizer.cullMode = VK_CULL_MODE_FRONT_BIT`.
text.d3d12: Cull the front faces instead: `CullMode = D3D12_CULL_MODE_FRONT`.

cull-front.hint: Now only the faces turned away from the camera are drawn: you look into the cubes, and the floor, whose front face points up, disappears.
